children: South Korea's top financial regulator said on Friday that it will build a tokenization infrastructure that can be applied to "all types" of securities, including stocks, bonds, and funds.

The announcement followed the third meeting of a consultative body on tokenized securities that took place on the same day. South Korea has passed amendments that legally recognize blockchain-based securities, set to take effect on Feb. 4, 2027.
The Financial Services Commission said the government has established a three-step plan to establish the infrastructure.

The first stage revolves around the securities token law taking effect in February. South Korea would start the tokenization of private money-market funds and private corporate bonds for institutional investors.

Tokenization of equities would begin with unlisted shares being tokenized through a trust, where the shares would stay on the existing system, and investors would receive a tokenized trust-beneficiary security.

If the first stage proves stable and successful, the second stage would expand the infrastructure to publicly offered securities. Stage three would establish an onchain settlement infrastructure that would allow investors to settle tokenized securities with stablecoins.
The FSC cited BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized fund and Hong Kong's tokenized green bonds as key references.
According to the latest release, existing securities brokerages and trading firms would be allowed to handle tokenized securities without requiring an additional license.

However, over-the-counter exchanges must consult the Financial Supervisory Service first, and retail investors on such platforms are subject to an annual net-purchase limit of 100 million won ($74,000) per venue.

The FSC also set registration rules for non-bank issuers that want to run investor accounts for their own token securities. Those institutions would need 4 billion won ($3 million) in equity capital and dedicated account, compliance, and IT staff.
